items.t: 정부, AIDC 진입 장벽 낮춘다…하위법령 입법예고 앞두고 기준 완화 가닥
items.d: 정부가 인공지능 데이터센터(AIDC) 인정 기준을 당초 논의된 시행령 초안보다 대폭 완화하는 방향으로 조정하는 것으로 확인됐다. 업계 의견을 반영해 AIDC 인정 범위를 넓히고, 기존 데이터센터의 일부를 AI용으로 전환하는 경우에도 AIDC로 인정받을 수 있도록 지원하려는 취지로 풀이된다. 1일 관련 업계에 따르면, 정부는 AIDC 특별법 하위법령 제정 작업을 마무리하고 이르면 이번 주 중 입법예고할 계획이다. AIDC 특별법은 AI 시대 핵심
items.fullText: AI·SW SW 정부, AIDC 진입 장벽 낮춘다…하위법령 입법예고 앞두고 기준 완화 가닥 발행일 : 2026-11-01 18:00 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 생성형 AI 이미지 정부가 인공지능 데이터센터(AIDC) 인정 기준을 당초 논의된 시행령 초안보다 대폭 완화하는 방향으로 조정하는 것으로 확인됐다. 업계 의견을 반영해 AIDC 인정 범위를 넓히고, 기존 데이터센터의 일부를 AI용으로 전환하는 경우에도 AIDC로 인정받을 수 있도록 지원하려는 취지로 풀이된다. 1일 관련 업계에 따르면, 정부는 AIDC 특별법 하위법령 제정 작업을 마무리하고 이르면 이번 주 중 입법예고할 계획이다. AIDC 특별법은 AI 시대 핵심 인프라가 될 AI 데이터센터의 확충을 촉진하고 국가 차원의 경쟁력을 확보하기 위해 제정됐다. 비수도권에 구축되는 AIDC에 대해 일정 요건을 충족할 경우 전력계통영향평가를 면제하는 등 특례를 부여한다. 데이터센터 구축 및 운영 과정에서의 인허가 부담을 줄이고 인프라 조기 확보를 돕는 것이 핵심 혜택이다. 당초 과기정통부는 시행령 초안에서 AIDC 인정 기준으로 두 가지를 제시했다. 첫 번째는 AI 연산 장비가 사용하는 전력 총량이 10메가와트(㎿) 이상인 경우다. AI 서버와 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 등 AI 연산에 쓰이는 장비의 전력 소비 규모가 일정 수준을 넘으면 AIDC로 인정하는 방식이다. 두 번째는 AI 장비의 전력 사용량이 최소 300킬로와트(㎾) 이상이면서 전체 정보통신 장비 전력의 60% 이상을 차지하는 경우다. 데이터센터 전체 정보통신 장비 가운데 AI 연산 장비가 차지하는 비중을 따져 AI 중심 시설인지를 판단하는 방식이다. 두 기준 중 하나만 충족하면 AIDC로 인정받을 수 있도록 설계했다. 정부는 이를 완화해 AI 장비 전력 총량 기준을 기존 10㎿에서 5㎿ 수준으로 낮추는 방안을 추진 중이다. 신축보다는 기존 데이터센터의 운영 방식 변화를 고려한 결정으로 보인다. 신축 데이터센터의 경우 10㎿ 기준 충족에 큰 무리가 없지만, 기존 데이터센터는 전체를 AI 전용으로 전환하기 어렵기 때문이다. 업계는 기존 센터의 일부를 AI용으로 전환하는 경우에도 AIDC로 인정받을 수 있도록 기준 완화를 요구해왔다. 비율 기준 또한 AI 장비 최소 전력 요건을 300㎾에서 250㎾로(GPU 약 280장 규모), 전체 정보통신 장비 전력에서 AI 장비가 차지하는 비중을 60%에서 50%로 각각 낮추는 방향으로 가닥을 잡았다. 신경망처리장치(NPU) 등이 설치되는 경우는 30% 등 별도 기준을 적용한다. 두 기준은 AI 데이터센터의 특성을 서로 다른 방식으로 판단한다. 전력 총량 기준은 전체 정보통신 장비에서 차지하는 비중과 관계없이 AI 장비전력량 기준을 넘으면 인정하는 방식이다. 비율 기준은 데이터센터 전체 정보통신 장비 가운데 AI 장비가 차지하는 비중을 따진다. 예를 들어 전체 정보통신 장비 전력이 1㎿라면 AI 장비전력 500㎾ 이상을 사용해야 50% 요건을 충족한다. 최소 전력 요건인 250㎾도 함께 만족해야 한다. 면제 상한을 두고는 과기정통부가 100㎿, 기후에너지환경부가 50㎿를 각각 제시해 협의 중이다. AI 인프라 확충 필요성과 산업계 의견을 고려해 100㎿ 수준을 추진하는 데 무게를 두고 있는 것으로 전해졌다. 과기정통부는 다음 주 초 산업계 의견을 수렴한 뒤 하위법령 입법예고에 나설 예정이다. 최호 기자 snoop@etnews.com 관련 기사 AIDC 가르는 '기술기준' 나왔다

items.t: Data centers are now a midterm issue, even in Brooklyn
items.d: At a Brooklyn midterm party five days before Election Day, every conversation, from a council member’s fireside chat to a debate about the Democratic Party, kept circling back to AI and data centers.
items.fullText: On Thursday evening, I slipped on my neon yellow heels and a floral mini dress. It’s New York, so I can wear whatever I want to a midterm election event full of media types, techies, policy advocates, and, well, does anyone else even exist at these things? I walked into the dimly blue-lit Brooklyn warehouse and was surprised to see the room already filling up. Newsreel, the media company founded by former Forbes and Newsweek reporter Jack Brewster, hosted the event, and the lineup was heavy-hitting. Kenneth Schlenker, co-founder of the focus app Opal, sat down for a fireside chat about “the state of attention,” and Aryan Banjan, who built the campaign management software Barza, gave a midterm forecast. I, meanwhile, was moderating a panel on data centers. Brewster said the goal was for people to “put their phones away and talk to each other about the election, five days out.” As the evening progressed, however, one topic consumed nearly every conversation: AI, data centers, and the backlash against the growing technocracy. Lately, as a tech reporter, I’ve noticed a growing chasm between tech and everyone else. I spend most of my days talking to people who see the benefits of AI, who are so ambitious in building it and so optimistic that it will succeed that, when I talk to people beyond the tech world, I forget how ugly it all seems to them. Outside the tech bubble, data centers and AI have become such an intense ballot-box issue that they could sway some midterm races on November 3. items.t: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
items.d: An NAACP lawsuit accuses the SpaceX-owned AI company of violating the Clean Air Act.
items.fullText: A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis. Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act. xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue. “Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision . Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.” TechCrunch has reached out to SpaceX for comment. In a statement , the NAACP’s director of environmental and climate justice Abre’ Connor described this as “another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable.” (A similar motion to dismiss from the Department of Justice was denied earlier this month ) “The courts have repeatedly rejected attempts by xAI and the DOJ to dismiss the NAACP’s Clean Air Act case, affirming our right to pursue justice for communities impacted by pollution,” Connor said. “Our position has been clear:

items.t: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
items.d: When investors get nervous about AI spending, it helps to have the chipmaker that sells the chips offer to cosign the loan.
items.fullText: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday . Bloomberg later corroborated the report. Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the project’s first building alone, according to Nscale’s IPO filing . In essence, the chipmaker would be co-signing a customer’s loans, a sign of how hard the AI industry is working to keep its buildout plans afloat as investors grow jittery about the amounts of money involved. The proposed arrangement would help Nscale secure financing for the electricity and construction costs of its West Virginia campus. Under what’s known as a residual value guarantee, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments, temporarily take over the facility, and help find a buyer and new tenant, according to The Information . Nvidia’s earlier support for cloud providers has mostly covered leases and chip purchases, not construction. The stakes are high for Nscale, which is seeking to go public at a valuation of up to $35 billion despite growing concerns about its ability to deliver on ambitious data center projects. Anthropic’s contract with Nscale covers the first 460-megawatt building at Nscale’s West Virginia campus, which is expected to use Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips. The companies are also discussing a second deal worth roughly $45 billion for another building. Nscale has struggled to get its projects off the ground. The company had about 25,000 advanced AI chips running in August , a fraction of the nearly 500,000 it plans to deploy. Its West Virginia campus has run into trouble of its own. Runoff from the construction site has flooded nearby homes more than once . In September, after months of negotiations , the project won state certification. This month, Microsoft pulled out of a planned Nscale site in England after grid power for it was pushed into the 2030s

items.t: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
items.d: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.
items.fullText: Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down. Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips. Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns. The anxiety spilled across the market on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and chip stocks took a drubbing, too: Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom more than 5%, and Qualcomm 11%. Alphabet, which plummeted 12% on Thursday, its worst day on record, wiping out $500 billion in market value, fell again. A big part of the concern is that companies that used to have overflowing free cash flow from their core businesses are getting hit as AI threatens the economics of those businesses. Alphabet provided the clearest example of that this week. Google’s parent company reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the third quarter, its second consecutive quarter in the red, even as quarterly capex grew to $51.4 billion. Alphabet expects to spend up to $205 billion this year, and expects that spending to keep rising in 2027. Meanwhile, the wild success of AI Mode — Google’s AI-powered chatbot feature built directly into Search — is eating into the company’s money-maker. Google’s Search advertising business, which makes up roughly half of its revenue, saw growth slow to 12%, its weakest pace in five quarters. That leaves Google walking a tightrope. items.t: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers
items.d: Satlyt ran a successful test this month bringing it closer to turning spacecraft, starting with satellites,  into virtual data centers.
items.fullText: Naturally, Rama Afullo’s first reaction was, “Let’s GOOOO,” he said. His company, Satlyt , is building software to turn existing satellites into data processing networks, similar to the orbital data center concept. And he just took another step closer to that. After 13 months of work, the company had a successful test earlier this month. Working with the University of Houston on a NASA-funded research project, the test showed how the startup’s software can spread out tasks among computers while in orbit based on communication and available compute. He said the goal is to create software that connects to multiple satellites to share computing assignments. Users of the system “will only need to define permissions, priorities, and operating limits,” while the software will make decisions within those limits, Afullo told TechCrunch. Its software is already on three satellites in orbit and the first step to that vision was this test. While the test used NASA-funded research, the agency has not yet selected it for any particular mission or chosen it to deploy its technology. Afullo said NASA missions face the same constraints that Satlyt hopes to address — “limited computing resources, intermittent communication, and the need to get useful information back to people.” In this test, the company created a simulated network with four computers, four users, and eight services. The software then assessed how to assign and run tasks on those computers, accounting for compute and communication availability. One physical computer aboard a spacecraft ran the experiment, evaluating a simulated network of four computing hosts, then returned the results to Earth. The test proved that Satlyt’s software can generate plans on hardware in orbit, but more testing will be done to see how those computers transfer information amongst each other in practice when multiple physical computers are used. “The finding is a trade-off,” he said. items.t: Google’s first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
items.d: The first TPU in space is running a Google DeepMind Gemma 4 model and writing cheesy poetry.
items.fullText: Google Suncatcher’s prototype space data center is online and communicating with the ground after launching earlier this month alongside more than 100 other spacecraft on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. The satellite, which carries four Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and generates up to 1 kW of electricity, is intended to pave the way for future networks of close-flying satellites performing large inference workloads in orbit. However, the power demands of the TPU mean it can only turn one on for about 20 minutes at a time, complicating the already tricky business of space-to-ground communications. After a commissioning process that tested out the satellite’s subsystems over about three weeks, the spacecraft was ready to work. When engineers on the ground sent their first prompt this week, they asked the model pre-loaded onto the satellite, Google DeepMind’s Gemma 4, to write a haiku about being in space. And thus: Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Google said it tested the model with these space-themed limericks (they should have sent a poet?) and, perhaps more importantly, the company asked the spacecraft to report on the orbital conditions around the satellite. A spokesperson told TechCrunch that the satellite was operating nominally. The ongoing test campaign will examine how the chips perform under thermal stress and in the space radiation environment. Google has extensively tested its TPUs in particle accelerators on Earth, but now needs to see how radiation’s real effects on their hardware in space affect their processor. Radiation can cause “bit flips” — causing a stored value in computer memory — and that in turn can corrupt data without triggering typical monitoring tools. items.t: Data center group jumps into the Kansas governor’s race to boost Republicans
items.d: Building the Future is an offshoot of the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future, arguably the leading super PAC promoting industry interests in the midterm elections.
items.fullText: FIRST ON NBC NEWS Artificial intelligence Artificial intelligence Data center group jumps into the Kansas governor’s race to boost Republicans Building the Future is an offshoot of the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future, arguably the leading super PAC promoting industry interests in the November midterm elections. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Kansas GOP gubernatorial candidate Ty Masterson at the Heartland Credit Union Arena in Park City, Kansas, a suburb of Wichita, on Oct. 19. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 26, 2026, 4:52 PM EDT By Allan Smith Building the Future, a new pro-data center super PAC, is spending more than $1.5 million to back Kansas state Sen. Ty Masterson, a Republican, in the state’s battle for governor , a person familiar with the spending said Monday in details first shared with NBC News. Building the Future is an offshoot of the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future, backed by AI heavyweights and arguably the leading super PAC promoting industry interests in the midterm elections. Earlier Monday, The New York Times reported that Building the Future is also set to spend about $1.5 million in advertising to boost GOP Sen. Darline Graham in the South Carolina Senate race. In August, Build American AI, a nonprofit that is also in the Leading the Future network, announced a multimillion-dollar ad campaign in Kansas, Ohio and Wisconsin seeking to boost preferred policies to govern data center growth. At the time, it announced the formation of the political group, Building the Future. items.fullText: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. items.fullText: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure Google Cloud A5X instances, accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, support European innovators with next-generation agentic and reinforcement learning infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Uttara Kumar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience.
